text: Ravi's payment just failed. Priya, the organizer, didn't chase him. Here's what her treasurer did next.
This is Turnkeeper, on PayPal.
Priya, a composite organizer, is her circle's bank, collector, and insurer.
Nineteen million US households are underbanked. In Sub-Saharan Africa, over a quarter of adults save in clubs.
Her rules, in Hindi, go in. Turnkeeper compiles them into a frozen charter: pot order, fees, quorum, and a hash.
Each member sees the fees up front, then approves the schedule once, on PayPal.
Three days out, the forecast flags Ravi. He paid late twice, and his last payday was three weeks before the due date. He gets a nudge in Hindi.
Round three runs on its own. Five charges complete, each confirmed through the PayPal Agent Toolkit. Ravi's is declined, and it's labelled sandbox-injected.
Ravi replies.
शुक्रवार को सैलरी आएगी, तब भर दूंगा।
Salary comes Friday. That becomes a promise with a date.
The agent proposes only what the charter allows. The buffer covers Ravi now, he repays by PayPal invoice, and he swaps turns with Tomas, so his pot comes last.
Both consent. Four of six vote yes. Priya taps once.
The agent reschedules the board, and sends Ravi an invoice with a QR code.
The ledger checks out, and PayPal Payouts sends Dev the pot, net of fees.
Round four is clean: six charges, one payout with PayPal's own IDs, and Priya typed nothing.
Under the hood, the model proposes, a policy engine decides, and humans approve where it matters.
On PayPal: Vault for consent, Orders for charges, Payouts for the pot, Invoicing through the Agent Toolkit, plus Webhooks and Balances.
The agent's tools sit behind an MCP server. A free model can drive them; this recording used the deterministic rules mode.
In a hundred rules-mode runs, ninety-five percent of proposals were charter-legal before the policy check, and zero illegal actions executed. A live free model: thirty-seven of thirty-seven legal.
And the full story ran end to end on the real PayPal sandbox.
PayPal's money pooling collects for one group purchase. Turnkeeper is the pool that rotates.
It's sandbox only. Fees are shown before anyone consents, the buffer is optional, and we make no credit claims.
Turnkeeper. Your circle, kept.
